newsitem.title: USA: Vishay looks at General Instrument unit.
newsitem.headline: Vishay looks at General Instrument unit.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology Inc said Tuesday it had a submitted a formal bid to buy Power Semiconductor, a division of General Instrument Corp.
The amount of the bid was not disclosed.
"This is Vishay's first attempt to enter the $14 billion discrete semiconductor market," it said in a press release.
Vishay company said it was one of several companies interested in buying the division, as had been reported by trade publications last week.

General Instrument's division makes power diodes, semiconductor components used to convert electrical currents from AC to DC and transient voltage suppressors, which protect equipment from voltage surges, it said.
It makes the diodes for the computer, telecommunications, automotive and consumer goods markets, generating sales of $360 million in 1996, it added.
General Instrument said earlier this month it was going to complete this summer its restructuring into three independent companies, one of them being General Semiconductor Inc.
Based in Malvern, Pennsylvania, Vishay passive electronic components.
